project_tracker_diagnostic: Evergreen/subevergreen shrub or small tree with narrow leathery leaves bearing a few coarse mucronate teeth, dark bark exfoliating in strips, and a shallow strongly tuberculate acorn cup.
verified_target_counties: Edwards; Real; Uvalde; Val Verde; Kerr; Bandera; Kimble; Kinney; Crockett

morphology_keys.habit: Evergreen or subevergreen shrub/small tree, commonly on dry limestone slopes and canyons.
morphology_keys.bark: Dark brown, furrowed, exfoliating in long strips.
morphology_keys.leaves: Narrowly lanceolate to oblong, leathery, usually with about 3–5 coarse teeth per side; teeth/lobes mucronate; underside densely stellate-hairy.
morphology_keys.acorn: Cup shallow, with strongly and regularly tuberculate scales; nut small, ovoid to oblong/subcylindric.
best_field_traits: FNA mature leaf 20–60(–90) × 10–20 mm; narrowly lanceolate/oblong, often 3–5 coarse mucronate-tipped teeth per side but sometimes entire.
Only 4–6 lateral veins on each side (often branching); lower surface generally densely covered with minute appressed stellate hairs.
Bud very small, about 1–1.5 mm; bark dark brown, furrowed, shedding in strips; twigs initially short-stellate hairy.
Acorn cup shallow, approximately 3–4 mm deep by 10 mm wide; cup scales reddish brown, markedly and evenly tuberculate; nut up to roughly 12 mm.
An old or shade leaf with an entire margin can resemble a live oak; examine bark, lateral veins, and the mature cup.

photo_strategy.oak_specific_tightening: Prioritize multi-photo late-summer/fall observations to increase the chance of mature leaves and acorns, plus curated taxon reference photos.

look_here_first: Check leathery evergreen to subevergreen NARROW leaves with a few large teeth (or entire margins), then dark bark peeling in long strips. Confirm a tiny shallow cup with strongly, regularly BUMPY/tuberculate scales; this beats leaf shape by itself.

diagnostic_comparison.method: Read habit, mature leaf and underside, bud, and ripe cupule together; avoid a single-leaf ID.

pair_specific_tie_breakers.quercus-sinuata-var-breviloba: White shin tends to have broader deciduous blades, 7–11 rather than 4–6 vein pairs, pale papery bark, and non-tuberculate flat cup scales.
pair_specific_tie_breakers.quercus-laceyi: Lacey leaves are commonly broader and distinctly glaucous, with the tip broad and rounded/retuse. Vasey has smaller, narrow, frequently toothed leaves and dark bark that peels in strips.
pair_specific_tie_breakers.quercus-fusiformis: Escarpment live oak is generally larger-leaved, often entire-margined, and bears a deeper acorn cup with spindle-like nut; Vasey has a small cup with regularly raised tubercles and 4–6 vein pairs. Juvenile live oak can be toothed.

diagnostic_comparison.field_uncertainty: Retain Quercus sp. or the pair-level comparison if intermediates / absent fruit prevent a reliable determination.
